content:
Data handling in Class 3 adds bar graphs to pictographs, tally marks and tables — careful-reading Olympiad questions. Here is what the Maths Olympiad Class 3 data handling chapter tests, the facts, the slips, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 3 Maths Olympiad Data Handling chapter tests

  • Reading pictographs and their key/scale
  • Reading bar graphs
  • Tally marks and tables
  • Interpreting data — most, fewest, how many more, totals

Key facts your child should know

  • In a pictograph, multiply the pictures by the key (a symbol may equal 2, 5 or 10).
  • On a bar graph, read a bar’s height off the scale.
  • A tally counts in fives; the fifth mark crosses the first four.
  • "How many more" is a subtraction; the total is the sum of every bar/row.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring the key or the scale.
  • Adding when the question asks how many more.
  • Misreading a bar between grid lines.

questions.q: A pictograph uses 1 face = 4 votes. Team Red has 6 faces and Team Blue has 9 faces. How many more votes has Blue?
On a bar graph, each 1 unit of height stands for 10. A bar is 4 units tall. What value does it show?
Trees planted by four houses: House P 16, House Q 28, House R 22, House S 34. Which house planted the fewest trees?
questions.explanation: House P planted only 16 trees, the least of the four.

questions.q: A pictograph shows toys made each day: Mon 15, Tue 20, Wed 10, Thu 25. What is the total number of toys?
In a pictograph 1 symbol = 6 story books, and a half symbol = 3. A row shows 4 full symbols and 1 half symbol. What is the total?
questions.explanation: 4 x 6 = 24, plus the half symbol worth 3: 24 + 3 = 27.

questions.q: 40 students voted for a favourite colour. Red got 15, Blue got 13, and the rest chose Green. How many chose Green?
A pictograph uses 1 symbol = 5 kites. If there are 9 symbols, how many kites are shown?
Heights (cm): 120, 135, 128, 142. Arranged from shortest to tallest, which comes third?
Marks scored: Amit 18, Ravi 24, Sara 15, Neha 21. Who scored the second highest?
questions.explanation: From highest to lowest: Ravi 24, Neha 21, Amit 18, Sara 15. The second highest is Neha (21).

questions.q: If 1 picture = 2 chocolates, how many pictures are needed to show 24 chocolates?

faq.q: How do you read a bar graph?
faq.a: Find the top of each bar and read the value off the scale on the side. The tallest bar is the most.

faq.q: What does a pictograph key mean?
faq.a: It tells you how many each picture stands for, so you multiply the pictures by the key to get the count.
